subject: Optimize: Cache hit-rate recommendations MVP — scope, launch criteria, resourcing
body:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nadia Rahman <nadia.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 13, 2025 at 9:14 AM PT
Subject: Optimize: Cache hit-rate recommendations MVP — scope, launch criteria, resourcing

Priya/Logan — following up on the Optimize “increase cache hit-rate” recommendations MVP.

I’m trying to lock:
1) MVP scope (what we ship vs. defer)
2) launch criteria / gating (what needs to be true before we turn it on)
3) who is doing the minimum telemetry/platform work to make the recs credible

Draft outline is here:
- Drive: shared_drives/product/optimize/cache-hit-rate-recommendations-mvp-outline
- Drive: shared_drives/engineering/console-and-tooling/recommendations-feed-api-contract

Proposed MVP (2–3 recommendation types only):
A) Prompt prefix diversity too high (normalization / templating guidance)
B) Routing fragmentation (same workload split across models/versions/routes -> cache fragmentation)
C) Cache policy mismatch (cache enabled but low cacheable prompt ratio / TTL too small / max_prefix_len mismatch)

Key principle: we should only show recs when we have enough evidence + we can link to the metric breakdown panel.

Telemetry inputs we believe we need for MVP (not per-request, aggregated):
- hit_rate (by route + model + version + region + deployment mode)
- hit_bytes and saved_prefill_ms (or a proxy) for “impact” ranking
- cacheable_prompt_ratio (so we don’t recommend normalization if workload isn’t cacheable)
- routing_fragmentation_score (can be heuristic based on distribution across model/version/route)
- prefix_diversity_score (heuristic; ok if v0 is coarse)

Launch criteria (proposal):
- v2 cache telemetry enabled for Hosted in us-west + us-east (flagged), stable for 7 days
- cardinality guardrails on (no tag explosion incidents) + dashboards show consistent hit_rate vs saved_prefill_ms correlation within expected range
- recommendation generator produces <5% “false positives” on internal dogfood routes (we can define this as: rec shown but top-3 evidence panels don’t support it)
- suppression controls available (per tenant/route), and a global kill-switch

Resourcing trade-off question: Do we have a Platform/Telemetry owner for the minimum “attribution stability” work? I’m trying to avoid Optimize shipping something that is immediately undermined by missing/partial tags.

If you can reply with: (1) accept/modify scope, (2) what you want as the gating bar, (3) which team can commit what in the next 2–3 weeks, I’ll update PM-912 + the rollout plan.

Thanks,
Aditya

—
Aditya Rao
Product, Redwood Optimize



From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nadia Rahman <nadia.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 13, 2025 at 10:02 AM PT
Subject: Re: Optimize: Cache hit-rate recommendations MVP — scope, launch criteria, resourcing

Agree with the principle (“only show recs with evidence + stable attribution”).

A few notes from telemetry side:

1) Impact ranking: saved_prefill_ms is the right north star for “this matters”, but it’s also the noisiest early on. I’d suggest for MVP we rank primarily on hit_bytes and use saved_prefill_ms as a secondary signal / displayed as “estimated”. (We can revisit once the runtime estimator is hardened.)

2) Prefix diversity: we need to be careful on cardinality. If the heuristic requires bucketing by hashed prefix, we should keep that inside the recommendation job, not as a metric tag. I’m +1 on “coarse is fine” v0.

3) Gating: 7 days might be ambitious if we’re rolling out v2 telemetry behind flags. I’d be comfortable with: “48 hours of stable ingestion + no tag explosion + alert noise below threshold” for internal dogfood, then staged external.

On ownership: Nadia can take point on the aggregation dataset for the recommendation engine (ENG-4815 adjacent) but we’ll need explicit acceptance criteria from Optimize for the inputs.

Can you put a short list of required fields + allowed null behavior? Example: if model_version is missing, do we suppress the rec or degrade to model-only?

- Logan



From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nadia Rahman <nadia.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 13, 2025 at 10:26 AM PT
Subject: Re: Optimize: Cache hit-rate recommendations MVP — scope, launch criteria, resourcing

This is directionally right, but we need to keep the MVP tight or it turns into “fix telemetry first” (which we’re already doing in the sprint).

Platform constraints / asks:
- Please don’t make model_version a hard requirement for MVP. Private + some Dedicated routes will be late to adopt the gateway tagging changes; we can’t block the feature on that.
- Do make “route” and “deployment_mode” required for any recommendation that appears. If we can’t attribute to a route, it’s not actionable.

Gating proposal from Platform:
1) Internal dogfood only until v2 telemetry is enabled + validated in us-west (Hosted) with cardinality guardrails.
2) External preview behind tenant allowlist (a handful of known-friendly customers) after 72 hours stable.
3) Expand to broader Hosted only after we have SRE sign-off that alerts are not noisy and data quality runbook is ready.

Resourcing: I can spare ~0.5 eng-week from Platform to help align the attribution fields / null-handling policy (Nadia + whoever is on the gateway side), but Optimize owns the user-facing contract.

Priya



From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nadia Rahman <nadia.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 13, 2025 at 11:11 AM PT
Subject: Re: Optimize: Cache hit-rate recommendations MVP — scope, launch criteria, resourcing

Thanks — super helpful.

Re: required fields / null behavior (proposed):

Hard requirements to show ANY rec:
- tenant_id (obviously)
- route_id (or route_name if that’s the stable dimension)
- deployment_mode
- region

Soft requirements (degrade gracefully):
- model + model_version: if version missing, compute fragmentation on model only and label the rec as “model-level (version data unavailable)”
- saved_prefill_ms: if missing/low confidence, show impact based on hit_bytes only

Suppress recs when:
- sample size too low (e.g., <N requests or <X tokens; will align with telemetry sampling rules)
- cacheable_prompt_ratio < threshold (for normalization recs)

On gating: I’m OK tightening the window to 48–72 hours of stable ingestion for dogfood and then allowlist preview.

Question for Logan/Nadia: what’s a realistic time estimate to produce an “Optimize-friendly” aggregated dataset/table so the recommendation job isn’t scraping raw metrics panels? If it’s 1–2 eng-weeks, we can plan around it. If it’s more, we should cut down to only 1 rec type for MVP.

Aditya



From: Nadia Rahman <nadia.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 13, 2025 at 12:03 PM PT
Subject: Re: Optimize: Cache hit-rate recommendations MVP — scope, launch criteria, resourcing

We can get you an aggregated dataset quickly if we keep the v0 requirements constrained.

Proposal:
- A daily (or hourly) rollup table keyed by: tenant_id, route_id, region, deployment_mode, model (optional), model_version (optional)
- Measures: request_count, token_count_prefill, token_count_decode, hit_bytes, miss_bytes, hit_rate (derived), cacheable_prompt_ratio (if available from gateway/runtime classification), saved_prefill_ms_est (nullable)

Timeline:
- 3–4 days to stand up schema + pipeline changes assuming v2 metrics are already flowing (ENG-4815 workstream)
- +2–3 days to validate against dashboards and add basic data quality checks (null rates, outliers)

Main risk: cacheable_prompt_ratio depends on runtime classification being consistently emitted; if that lags, we can still ship the other two rec types and gate normalization recs behind “classification coverage > 90%” for that tenant/route.

If this works, please confirm:
- do you want hourly or daily? (hourly increases compute, but better for “recent regression” messaging)
- do you need per-route top-N model versions or just the dominant one? (top-N increases output size)

Nadia



From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Nadia Rahman <nadia.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 13, 2025 at 1:18 PM PT
Subject: Re: Optimize: Cache hit-rate recommendations MVP — scope, launch criteria, resourcing

From Console side: please prefer hourly rollups if possible.

Reason: we want the recommendations feed to feel “alive” during staged rollout and oncall validation, and we want to be able to say “in the last 6h, cache hit-rate dropped” without doing weird client-side math.

Also, for the API contract, we need:
- evidence links that resolve to a specific dashboard view (route + region + deployment mode pre-filtered)
- a “why am I seeing this?” explainer string that is stable for support tickets

If hourly is too expensive, we can do daily for GA but hourly for dogfood/allowlist preview.

Marissa



From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Nadia Rahman <nadia.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 14, 2025 at 4:37 PM PT
Subject: Re: Optimize: Cache hit-rate recommendations MVP — scope, launch criteria, resourcing

OK — aligning on the following, unless anyone objects by EOD Monday:

MVP scope (ship):
1) Routing fragmentation rec (route split across models/versions/routes)
2) Cache policy mismatch rec (cache enabled but low hit_rate + low cacheable_prompt_ratio OR suspected TTL/max_prefix_len mismatch)
3) Prompt normalization rec is “conditional”: only shown when cacheable_prompt_ratio classification coverage is high enough (Nadia’s suggested 90%+ coverage threshold)

Data model:
- Hourly rollup for dogfood + allowlist preview; revisit daily for GA if cost is an issue.
- Required dims to show rec: tenant_id, route_id, region, deployment_mode.
- Optional dims: model, model_version.

Launch gating:
- Stage 0: internal dogfood only after 48–72h stable ingestion in us-west (Hosted) + cardinality guardrails on.
- Stage 1: external allowlist preview after 72h stable + basic data quality checks (null rates, outliers) + Console evidence links working.
- Stage 2: broader Hosted expansion only after SRE sign-off (alerts not noisy + runbook in place).

Resourcing:
- Telemetry (Nadia/Logan): rollup table + data quality checks (target 1–1.5 weeks elapsed)
- Optimize: recommendation generator + copy + suppression/kill switch semantics (PM-912)
- Platform: attribution/null-handling alignment (~0.5 eng-week per Priya)

Next steps:
- I’ll update PM-912 with the above + acceptance criteria.
- Nadia: please comment in PM-912 with the proposed schema + whether hourly is viable for preview.
- Priya/Logan: please confirm this gating is acceptable (or call out any red flags) so I can treat it as a decision.

Thanks all,
Aditya

—
Aditya Rao
Product, Redwood Optimize
